summary: Learn the critical links between climate change and the Water-Energy-Food Nexus. Enroll in our training course to empower your understanding and impact.
lede: Water-energy-food nexus planning examines how climate risks and decisions in one system affect the others. For professionals in climate adaptation, resource management, energy, agriculture, and program delivery, the course offers practical ways to assess vulnerabilities and choose coordinated interventions. Participants practice mapping dependencies, analyzing trade-offs and synergies, and prioritizing options with decision tools across water, energy, and food systems.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals across various sectors who are responsible for integrated planning under climate risk conditions.
audience: Water resource managers and WASH leads
Energy planners, utilities, and renewable energy teams
Agriculture and food security program staff
NGO program managers and technical advisors
Donor-funded project teams and grant managers
Sustainability, ESG, and corporate responsibility leads
Disaster risk reduction and humanitarian coordination staff
modules: Trade-Offs and Synergies in Real Decisions
Climate-Smart Water Management in the Nexus
Energy Systems and Resilience for Water and Food
Food Systems Resilience and Climate Adaptation
Financing, Investment Cases, and Value for Resilience
Monitoring, Indicators, and Learning Across Sectors
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of climate change impacts, resource management, and sector-specific challenges. Experience in program or project management, policy development, or technical advisory roles is beneficial but not mandatory.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
